text:
Linus Karlsson took the long road to a regular job: a third-round pick by San Jose in 2018, a stop in the SHL, an AHL season in Abbotsford, and only 106 NHL games before this one. Now he's one of the more quietly useful forwards in Vancouver. Sunday in Las Vegas he went around Shea Theodore and roofed one over Carter Hart's glove, then added an empty-netter as the Canucks snapped a seven-game skid.

His 12 points in 23 games look ordinary until you see where he plays. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting 6.7 scoring chances per 60 from the home-plate area in front of the net last season, 88th percentile, and Evolving-Hockey rated him a play driver, worth 1.6 wins with teammates in the bottom 3% by impact.

That last part is the catch now, too: Vancouver gets just 40% of the expected goals at five-on-five with him on the ice, roughly what it gets without him. He's carrying a line more than lifting it. If the Canucks find him better linemates, the points could follow the chances.
headline: Karlsson keeps getting to the good ice
